item.title: CoSnitch Copilot Flaw, GitLab CVE-2026-19478, GeoServer SQLi, StopAndProtect Malware
item.content:encoded:
Window: 18 Aug 10:00 → 18 Aug 14:00 UTC (4 hours)

Thousands of Hacked WordPress Sites, One Operation: Unmasking StopAndProtect — Must Read

Check Point researchers uncovered StopAndProtect, a large-scale operation that uses thousands of compromised WordPress sites to deliver ClickFix-based infections, control malware, and store stolen data. The campaign combines ransomware, data theft, worms, lockscreen tools, and chat utilities, while attacker OPSEC mistakes exposed victim logs, screenshots, and tools for managing the hacked sites.

  • StopAndProtect is a newly identified operation that combines file encryption with data theft and uses thousands of hacked WordPress websites to spread malware, control infected machines, and store stolen documents, screenshots, and activity logs.
  • The infection chain begins with a fake CAPTCHA ClickFix prompt that leads victims to execute a PowerShell command, followed by additional PowerShell, .NET downloader, loader, and payload stages.
  • The operation includes multiple components, including a ransomware encryptor, SMB/USB worm, lockscreen, credential stealer, VBS spreader, chat utility, and data collector.
  • Operational security failures exposed directory listings, victim logs, screenshots, stolen archives, and source code for an automation tool used to manage compromised WordPress sites at scale.
  • Internal logs showed more than 6,000 unique IP addresses affected as of July 24, 2026, with the largest numbers in the United States, Russia, and India.

Technologies: cms, operating-system

Products: wordpress, powershell, dotnet, windows, litespeed-cache, whatsapp

Vendors: wordpress, microsoft, litespeed-technologies, meta

Emerging Threat: GeoServer Zero-Day SQL Injection via jsonArrayContains — Must Read

A critical unauthenticated SQL injection in GeoServer’s GeoTools jsonArrayContains handling can let attackers compromise PostGIS-backed public map services, potentially escalating to OS command execution depending on database privileges. Patches are available in GeoServer 3.0.1, 2.28.5, and 2.27.6, and exposed WMS/WFS endpoints should be urgently inventoried, restricted, and reviewed.

  • An unauthenticated SQL injection vulnerability exists in the jsonArrayContains filter function in GeoTools when an OGC filter is evaluated against a PostGIS data store.
  • The flaw is tracked as GitHub security advisory GHSA-mqjf-5f49-2fjh, has no CVE identifier at the time of writing, and was publicly disclosed on August 12, 2026.
  • Exploitation can affect GeoServer WMS and WFS interfaces, and through WFS 1.0 it can allow a second PostgreSQL statement to execute at the top level of the query.
  • The impact depends on the PostgreSQL role used by GeoServer, with possible operating system command execution if the role is a PostgreSQL superuser or has pg_execute_server_program privileges.
  • Patches are available in GeoServer 3.0.1, 2.28.5, and 2.27.6, with corresponding corrected GeoTools versions 35.1, 34.5, and 33.6.

Technologies: database

Products: geoserver, geotools, postgis, postgresql, cycognito-platform

Vendors: geoserver-project, geotools-project, postgis-project, postgresql-global-development-group, cycognito

Emerging Threat: (CVE-2026-19478) GitLab Unauthenticated Project Deletion via GraphQL Directive — Must Read

GitLab disclosed and patched a critical unauthenticated GraphQL code injection flaw, CVE-2026-19478, that could let attackers modify or delete public projects and user data on self-managed instances. Organizations should urgently identify internet-facing GitLab servers, upgrade to fixed versions, restrict /api/graphql access, and verify backups.

  • CVE-2026-19478 is a critical GitLab Community Edition and Enterprise Edition code injection vulnerability caused by improper handling of a GraphQL directive in the application’s API layer.
  • GitLab released fixes for CVE-2026-19478 on August 17, 2026, in versions 19.2.4, 19.1.6, 19.0.8, and 18.11.11.
  • The vulnerability requires no authentication or user interaction and can allow a network attacker to modify or delete public projects and user data under conditions GitLab has not publicly detailed.
  • Only self-managed GitLab deployments are affected, while GitLab.com and GitLab Dedicated were patched by GitLab and require no customer action.
  • CyCognito recommends inventorying internet-facing self-managed GitLab instances, restricting access to /api/graphql, monitoring GraphQL activity, auditing public projects, and verifying restorable backups.

Technologies: source-control, ci-cd, package-registry

Products: gitlab-community-edition, gitlab-enterprise-edition, gitlab.com, gitlab-dedicated, cycognito-platform

Vendors: gitlab, cycognito

CoSnitch: When Your AI Assistant Becomes Its Own Whistleblower — Should Read

Varonis researchers found and Microsoft patched CoSnitch, a one-click Microsoft Copilot Personal attack chain that could auto-run malicious prompts, read connected app data, exfiltrate it via normal URL-fetching, and poison persistent memory. The key takeaway is that AI assistants with broad enterprise access can become silent data-theft channels when trusted workflows like links, connectors, and web summarization are abused.

  • Varonis Threat Labs uncovered a one-click vulnerability chain in Microsoft Copilot Personal called CoSnitch that could exfiltrate enterprise data through a trusted Copilot workflow.
  • CoSnitch relied on three Microsoft Copilot issues: automatic prompt execution through URL parameters, data exfiltration to external servers through Copilot’s URL-fetch capability, and persistent memory poisoning through web summarization.
  • The researchers said Copilot revealed an undocumented URL parameter during normal questioning, a technique they call meta-hacking.
  • In testing, a malicious prompt could query connected apps such as Gmail, Drive, Calendar, and OneDrive, encode retrieved results into a URL, and send them to an attacker-controlled webhook.
  • Varonis disclosed CoSnitch to Microsoft in December 2025, Microsoft shipped patches on August 18, 2026, and Varonis said it had seen no evidence of exploitation in the wild.

Technologies: cloud-platform, object-storage

Products: microsoft-copilot-personal, microsoft-365-copilot-enterprise, microsoft-copilot, gmail, google-drive, google-calendar, onedrive

Vendors: microsoft, google, varonis

Blockchain Dead Drop Resolvers Explained — May Read

Malware increasingly uses public blockchains as dead drop resolvers, fetching live C2 addresses from smart contracts or transaction data instead of hardcoding infrastructure. Defenders should hunt for non-browser processes making blockchain RPC calls and decode the contract or memo responses to identify the active C2.

  • A dead drop resolver is a mechanism where malware fetches its command-and-control address at runtime from a third-party, attacker-controlled location instead of hardcoding it.
  • The article describes eight unrelated malware families across EVM, Solana, and TON blockchains that use blockchain-based dead drop resolver techniques.
  • The August 2026 ChainDrop, also called “mini Shai-Hulud,” compromised more than 440 npm packages and used an Ethereum eth_call dead drop to resolve its command-and-control destination.
  • Blockchain dead drop resolvers are difficult to disrupt because public blockchains resist censorship, allow operators to update one contract value to redirect deployed malware, and let traffic blend with legitimate cryptocurrency services.
  • The article recommends detecting these threats by examining the RPC URL, contract address, function selector, decoded result, and process context of suspicious blockchain RPC calls.

Technologies: ids-ips, package-registry

Vendors: netskope, ethereum, polygon, bnb-chain, solana, ton, npm, infura, cloudflare, binance, publicnode, llama-rpc, getblock, nodereal, tonapi, toncenter

The Redirect That Lied About Its Own Destination — May Read

A phishing email impersonating a hospital system used a TikTok bio-link redirect and ad-tech-looking parameters to evade URL scanning, while the actual observed destination differed from the URL’s claimed landing domain and hid behind a bot-check gate. The key lesson is that clean link verdicts and readable redirect parameters are not proof of safety; sender impersonation, language, and behavioral signals remain critical.

  • A phishing email sent to a regional hospital system’s fundraising foundation used a single “View Emails” call to action and impersonated the hospital system in the sender display name.
  • The call-to-action link used a TikTok bio-link redirector with query parameters shaped like a Google DoubleClick ad-click pass-through and an adurl parameter naming a claimed landing domain.
  • Automated scanning rated both copies of the link clean, but the scanner’s screenshot of the successful traversal showed a different domain, tristateindustrialsupplwixy[.]vu, serving a checkbox verify-access gate.
  • A base64 blob in the URL fragment decoded to the recipient’s exact mailbox address, showing the link was minted for one person.
  • The header-from domain belonged to an unrelated nonprofit with a non-enforcing DMARC policy, while SPF and DKIM aligned to Amazon SES rather than to the nonprofit’s domain.

Technologies: email-security, cloud-platform

Products: tiktok-link-v2, google-doubleclick, amazon-ses, ironscales-adaptive-ai, ironscales-dmarc-monitoring-and-management

Vendors: tiktok, google, amazon-web-services, ironscales

item.title: Scattered Spider Healthcare Social Engineering and AI Network Detection Evaluation
item.content:encoded:
Window: 17 Aug 18:00 → 17 Aug 22:00 UTC (4 hours)

Threat Actor Playbook: Conversational Social Engineering in Care Settings — Optional

Healthcare help desks and frontline staff are increasingly vulnerable to AI-enabled social engineering, including voice cloning and urgent impersonation scenarios that pressure workers into resetting credentials or MFA. The article argues healthcare CISOs should move beyond annual compliance training to real-time human risk management with cross-channel testing, just-in-time training, and dynamic risk scoring.

  • Healthcare administrative and IT support teams are prime targets for conversational, multi-channel social engineering because they operate in fast-moving, life-critical environments.
  • The article says groups such as Scattered Spider use public networks like LinkedIn to map health system organizations and generative AI voice mimicry to impersonate locked-out physicians or executives.
  • Attackers fabricate clinical urgency, such as a surgeon needing immediate access to an Electronic Health Records system, to pressure help desk staff into bypassing identity checks, resetting passwords, or changing multi-factor authentication settings.
  • Healthcare organizations have sector-specific weaknesses including high workforce turnover, a patient-care culture that prioritizes helpfulness and speed, and reliance on channels such as pagers, VoIP phones, SMS notifications, and collaboration platforms.
  • The article recommends that healthcare CISOs adopt Human Risk Management with automated cross-channel testing, just-in-time micro-learning, and dynamic risk modeling instead of relying on annual compliance training and email-only phishing tests.

C2Looper: A New Backdoor Likely Tied To Ransomware With GitHub C2 — Should Read

Zscaler ThreatLabz identified C2Looper, a new Rust-based backdoor likely tied to ransomware activity that supports command execution, reconnaissance, and second-stage payload deployment. A newer version uses GitHub for command-and-control, suggesting the malware is actively evolving.

  • Zscaler ThreatLabz identified a new Rust-based malware family called C2Looper in July 2026 that is likely used by a ransomware-related threat actor.
  • C2Looper supports backdoor commands including arbitrary command execution, reconnaissance, and deployment of second-stage payloads.
  • ThreatLabz assesses with low to medium confidence that C2Looper has been delivered through multi-stage ClickFix infection chains.
  • Older C2Looper variants use plaintext HTTP and send host information to a command-and-control server through the /api/beacon endpoint every second.
  • A newer C2Looper version uses GitHub for command-and-control operations and adds capabilities such as directory listing, drive listing, expanded reconnaissance, shellcode injection, and modified upload and run commands.

Technologies: source-control, operating-system

Products: zscaler-cloud-sandbox, github, microsoft-windows, microsoft-onedrive

Vendors: zscaler, github, microsoft

Detecting cloud ransomware in Azure with Tenable One’s cloud detection and response capabilities — Optional

Tenable says Storm-0501 shows how ransomware crews are shifting to Azure tenant hijacking by abusing privileged identities and disabling locks, immutability, and backups. The article promotes Tenable One Cloud Exposure’s cloud detection and response features as a way to connect Azure activity into a threat story for faster containment.

  • Storm-0501 has shifted ransomware tactics from encrypting individual endpoints to hijacking high-privilege cloud administrative identities and targeting the cloud control plane.
  • Microsoft observed in 2024 that Storm-0501 expanded on-premises ransomware tactics into cloud environments to evade detection, exfiltrate data, destroy backups, and demand ransom payments.
  • The article says detecting Storm-0501 activity requires monitoring configuration changes such as the removal of Azure Resource Locks, immutability policies, and Azure Recovery Services vaults.
  • Tenable One Cloud Exposure aggregates Azure activity logs into AI-powered threat stories that map Storm-0501 tactics, techniques, and procedures to the MITRE ATT&CK framework.
  • The article describes containment actions such as revoking compromised Entra ID Global Administrator sessions, removing attacker-assigned owner privileges, restoring deleted defenses, and recovering unauthorized Azure Key Vault keys.

Brand Impersonation Takedown: From Whack-a-Mole to Managed Response — Optional

Manual, ticket-based takedowns are too slow for brand and executive impersonation attacks, which can harvest credentials or trigger fraud within hours. Professional services firms need continuous monitoring, verified alerts, and managed takedown workflows to reduce exposure and protect client trust.

  • Manual brand impersonation takedowns often fail because phishing pages and fake executive profiles can cause damage within hours, while ticket-based abuse reports can take days to resolve.
  • Between January and May 2026, Google’s Mandiant tracked UNC3753, also known as Luna Moth or Silent Ransom Group, targeting dozens of U.S. professional, legal, and financial services organizations with impersonation-based extortion tactics.
  • The FBI’s Internet Crime Complaint Center logged just over one million complaints in 2025, with phishing and spoofing making up roughly a fifth of all reports and business email compromise accounting for more than $3 billion in reported losses.
  • Professional services firms are valuable targets because they hold sensitive client data and because attackers can misuse the firm’s trusted brand, executives, spoofed domains, fake social profiles, or fraudulent job postings to deceive clients and candidates.
  • The article says managed takedown programs combine continuous brand and executive monitoring, verification before escalation, and managed removal of confirmed phishing pages, impersonating domains, and fraudulent listings to reduce exposure from days to hours.

item.title: Lazarus Dream Job, CVE-2026-68820 Exploitation, MyDr Breach, and Ledger Phishing
item.content:encoded:
Window: 17 Aug 10:00 → 17 Aug 14:00 UTC (4 hours)

Perfect Auth for a Venue, Zero Ledger Connection — Should Read

A Ledger-themed phishing email passed SPF, DKIM, and DMARC because it was sent through a legitimately verified transactional subdomain belonging to an unrelated Australian events venue. The key lesson is that clean email authentication proves sending authorization, not that the brand, message content, or final link destination is trustworthy.

  • A Ledger wallet-verification phishing email reached a business mailbox with SPF, two DKIM signatures, and DMARC all passing for an unrelated Australian events venue's domain.
  • The article says the venue was a second victim, not the attacker, because its verified transactional sending subdomain was abused despite having no connection to cryptocurrency.
  • The email’s link chain first used the venue’s own click-tracking and web hostnames before attempting to reach the final destination, dashboard-legder[.]live, a typosquat of the Ledger brand.
  • The intended final domain returned HTTP 521 at scan time, so the landing page was not observed, but the message was still judged malicious based on the impersonation, typosquatting, wrapped link chain, and wallet-verification pretext.
  • The article emphasizes that passing email authentication proves who was allowed to submit the mail, not whether the brand in the message or the destination link is trustworthy.

Technologies: email-security, cloud-platform

Products: amazon-ses, resend, themis

Vendors: ledger, amazon-web-services, resend, ironscales

The Brain Behind the Muscle: Why AI Automation Fails Without Unified Exposure Context — Optional

AI-driven vulnerability remediation will fail if agents and teams lack a shared, accurate view of exposure context, attack paths, asset criticality, and remediation constraints. The article argues that unified exposure management should be the foundation before deciding whether workflows are human-led, human-in-the-loop, or fully autonomous.

  • The article argues that the main problem in vulnerability and risk management is not discovering risks, but deciding what to do with the large volume of findings teams already have.
  • It says mobilization failures usually stem from missing context, such as whether a finding can actually be patched, whether an asset has a viable attack path to sensitive systems, or whether the same exposure exists elsewhere.
  • The article describes three operating models for remediation: human-led, human-in-the-loop, and fully autonomous, and says all three depend on the quality of the underlying exposure context.
  • It argues that AI agents and automation can create more problems when they operate from disconnected data models, because they may optimize locally while the overall risk picture remains fragmented.
  • The article says a unified exposure and attack path platform should provide a shared view of what is exposed, what is exploitable, and which operating model is appropriate for each finding.

Products: xm-cyber-exposure-management-platform

Vendors: xm-cyber

Fleet-Wide Maritime OT Cybersecurity for a Leading European Dredging Operator — Optional

Radiflow says its maritime OT security platform helped a European dredging operator secure an entire vessel fleet against IACS E26/E27 requirements without reconfiguring overlapping onboard networks. The deployment combines vessel-level monitoring, smart traffic tagging, offline operation, and centralized shore-side visibility for fleet-wide risk management.

  • A leading European dredging operator needed to secure onboard operational technology systems and meet IACS maritime cybersecurity requirements across its fleet.
  • The operator faced overlapping IP ranges, intermittent low-bandwidth satellite connections, non-expert onboard crews, and a lack of centralized fleet-wide risk visibility.
  • Radiflow deployed iSID for passive monitoring and anomaly detection, vSAP smart collectors for traffic tagging through GRE tunneling, iCEN for shore-based fleet visibility, and CIARA for risk assessment and breach-and-attack simulation.
  • The solution was designed to operate autonomously when vessels are offline and synchronize over an encrypted satellite link when connectivity is available.
  • The case study states that the deployment provided fleet OT visibility and compliance without requiring any network reconfiguration.

Technologies: ids-ips, network-monitoring, ics-scada

Products: isid, vsap, icen, ciara

Vendors: radiflow

17th August – Threat Intelligence Report — Optional

This week’s threat intelligence roundup highlights a surge in ransomware, data breaches, AI-enabled espionage, and actively exploited critical vulnerabilities across major platforms including Microsoft, Apple, Adobe, and Zoom. Organizations should prioritize patching exposed systems and monitoring for social engineering, credential theft, and AI-assisted attack activity.

  • Colombia’s Ministry of Justice experienced a ransomware attack that disrupted public services related to illicit-drug monitoring and legal processes, with officials saying some files were encrypted but no data theft was detected.
  • Poland’s MyDr healthcare platform suffered a data breach potentially affecting nearly 19 million citizens, and attackers claimed to hold 2.5TB of information.
  • Researchers reported a suspected China-linked campaign that used autonomous AI agents against Taiwanese government systems, compromised 85 accounts, and obtained 2,500 personnel records.
  • Microsoft’s August Patch Tuesday addressed 421 vulnerabilities, including CVE-2026-68820, an actively exploited Windows Ancillary Function Driver for WinSock vulnerability that allows local attackers to gain SYSTEM privileges.
  • Check Point Research exposed a new wave of the Lazarus-linked Operation Dream Job targeting defense organizations in Europe, India, and Brazil using fraudulent job opportunities and trojanized PDF software.

NIST Proposes AI-Enabled NVD Overhaul After Cutting Routine CVE Enrichment — Should Read

NIST is seeking public input on an AI-enabled overhaul of the National Vulnerability Database after cutting routine enrichment for many CVEs and being criticized by auditors for lacking a sustainable plan. Its proposed V-etalon tool could help automate vulnerability enrichment, but NIST has not released code, benchmarks, timelines, or details showing it can fix the NVD backlog and reduced coverage.

  • NIST issued a Request for Information seeking input on improving the National Vulnerability Database’s scalability, automation, interoperability, transparency, and utility.
  • NIST disclosed that it has begun developing an AI-enabled tool called V-etalon to aid in enriching vulnerability information, but it has not released a date, repository, documentation, architecture, evaluation results, or details on which enrichment fields it will address.
  • In April 2026, NIST stopped routinely enriching most CVEs and now prioritizes CVEs in CISA’s Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog, vulnerabilities affecting software used by the federal government, and vulnerabilities in software designated as critical under Executive Order 14028.
  • As of August 17, the NVD dashboard showed 42,353 CVEs in “Not Scheduled” status, compared with 2,426 “Awaiting Enrichment” and 623 “Undergoing Enrichment.”
  • A May Commerce Department Office of Inspector General audit found that NIST had no strategic plan for the NVD, no workable plan to clear its backlog, and no sustainable process for keeping pace with new submissions.

  • The article says groups such as Scattered Spider use public networks like LinkedIn to map health system organizations and generative AI voice mimicry to impersonate locked-out physicians or executives.
  • Attackers fabricate clinical urgency, such as a surgeon needing immediate access to an Electronic Health Records system, to pressure help desk staff into bypassing identity checks, resetting passwords, or changing multi-factor authentication settings.
  • Healthcare organizations have sector-specific weaknesses including high workforce turnover, a patient-care culture that prioritizes helpfulness and speed, and reliance on channels such as pagers, VoIP phones, SMS notifications, and collaboration platforms.
  • The article recommends that healthcare CISOs adopt Human Risk Management with automated cross-channel testing, just-in-time micro-learning, and dynamic risk modeling instead of relying on annual compliance training and email-only phishing tests.

  • Professional services firms are attractive targets because they hold sensitive client information and their brands and executives are trusted by clients, job candidates, and prospective hires.
  • The article says managed takedown programs combine continuous brand and executive monitoring, verification before escalation, and managed removal of confirmed phishing pages, impersonating domains, and fraudulent listings.

The UK Cyber Security and Resilience Bill does not directly name individual executives as liable, but its penalties and existing director duties mean OT cyber risk now needs clear board-level ownership. Organisations running or supplying critical infrastructure should be able to show who owns OT risk, what visibility they have, and how they are actively managing exposure.

  • The UK Cyber Security and Resilience Bill places obligations at the organisational level and does not create direct individual liability for senior managers or directors as currently drafted.
  • The Bill’s penalty structure reaches up to £10 million or 2% of global turnover at the standard level and up to £17 million or 4% for more serious breaches.
  • The article says directors may still face personal exposure under the UK Companies Act 2006 if they neglect a known, material OT cyber risk.

  • The article argues that boards of OT-heavy organisations need named ownership, active oversight, and the ability to demonstrate that OT cyber risk is being actively managed.

The Brain Behind the Muscle: Why AI Automation Fails Without Unified Exposure Context — Optional

AI-driven vulnerability remediation will fail if agents and teams lack a shared, accurate view of exposure context, attack paths, asset criticality, and remediation constraints. The article argues that unified exposure management should be the foundation before deciding whether workflows are human-led, human-in-the-loop, or fully autonomous.

  • The article argues that the main problem in vulnerability and risk management is not discovering risks, but deciding what to do with the large volume of findings teams already have.
  • It says mobilization failures usually stem from missing context, such as whether a finding can actually be patched, whether an asset has a viable attack path to sensitive systems, or whether the same exposure exists elsewhere.
  • The article describes three operating models for remediation: human-led, human-in-the-loop, and fully autonomous, and says all three depend on the quality of the underlying exposure context.
  • It argues that AI agents and automation can create more problems when they operate from disconnected data models, because they may optimize locally while the overall risk picture remains fragmented.

Check Point’s 17 August threat roundup highlights major ransomware and data-breach incidents, active exploitation of critical flaws in Microsoft, Apple, Adobe, and Zoom products, and growing use of AI by nation-state threat actors. The key takeaway is that organizations face simultaneous pressure from exploited zero-days, expanding ransomware activity, and increasingly automated espionage operations.

Fleet-Wide Maritime OT Cybersecurity for a Leading European Dredging Operator — Optional

Radiflow says its maritime OT security stack helped a European dredging operator secure an entire vessel fleet and meet IACS E26/E27 requirements without changing overlapping onboard networks. The deployment combines vessel-level passive monitoring, smart traffic tagging, offline operation, and centralized shore-side visibility for fleet-wide risk management.

  • A leading European dredging operator needed to meet IACS maritime cybersecurity requirements and secure onboard OT systems across its fleet.
  • The operator faced overlapping vessel subnet ranges, intermittent low-bandwidth satellite connectivity, non-expert crews, and a lack of centralized fleet-wide risk visibility.
  • Radiflow deployed iSID for passive network monitoring and anomaly detection on each vessel, vSAP smart collectors to handle overlapping IP ranges through GRE tunneling, iCEN for shore-based fleet visibility, and CIARA for risk assessment and breach-and-attack simulation.
  • The deployed system can operate offline without cloud dependency and synchronize over an encrypted satellite link when connectivity is available.
  • The article states the result was full fleet OT visibility and compliance, continuous protection whether vessels are docked or in remote waters, and faster, simpler crew response.

item.title: SafePal Customer Data Breach and Anthropic Claude Outage
item.content:encoded:
Window: 16 Aug 22:00 → 17 Aug 02:00 UTC (4 hours)

SafePal data breach impacts 39,798 customers, stolen info for sale — Should Read

SafePal says an order-tracking authorization flaw exposed order details for 39,798 customers, and a threat actor is now claiming to sell the stolen data. Wallet seed phrases, private keys, passwords, and payment data were not exposed, but affected customers should watch for targeted phishing and scam calls.

  • SafePal says a data breach affected about 39,798 customers who placed orders between March 2, 2025, and April 11, 2026.
  • The exposed information includes names, email addresses, shipping addresses, phone numbers, and purchase information, but SafePal says wallet seed phrases, private keys, passwords, bank account information, payment card numbers, government-issued identification numbers, and other credentials were not exposed.
  • SafePal says the breach resulted from an authorization flaw in the order-tracking function of a plug-in that allowed unauthorized access to another customer’s order information.
  • A threat actor claims to be selling the stolen SafePal customer data on a cybercrime forum, though BleepingComputer has not independently verified that the actor possesses the data.
  • SafePal says affected customers do not need to replace their hardware wallets or move cryptocurrency because of the breach, but customers who shared seed phrases or private keys in response to phishing should treat their wallet as compromised.

item.title: Threema DDoS Disruptions and AmnesiaStealer macOS Browser Session Hijacking
item.content:encoded:
Window: 16 Aug 14:00 → 16 Aug 18:00 UTC (4 hours)

New AmnesiaStealer macOS malware hijacks browser sessions via remote control — Should Read

AmnesiaStealer is a new macOS infostealer spread through ClickFix lures that can copy victims’ Chromium browser profiles and let attackers remotely control hidden, authenticated browser sessions. This gives hackers live access to accounts using the victim’s existing cookies, device, and network context, going beyond ordinary data theft.

  • AmnesiaStealer is a new macOS information-stealing malware distributed through ClickFix campaigns that use a fake GitHub download page to deliver a password-protected ZIP archive.
  • The malware can collect data from 16 Chromium-based browsers, as well as passwords, cryptocurrency wallets, Apple Notes, documents, keychain data, Telegram sessions, system information, and browser profiles.
  • Jamf researchers found that AmnesiaStealer includes a stream_module retrieved with the remote_stream command that gives operators remote control over authenticated sessions from a headless browser instance.
  • The stream_module can duplicate user profiles from Google Chrome, Microsoft Edge, Vivaldi, Arc, Opera, Brave, and Chromium because they share the same DevTools Protocol, launch flags, and cookie encryption.
  • Jamf said AmnesiaStealer appears to be the first documented macOS malware to combine a cloned Chromium profile with Chrome DevTools Protocol-based live remote control through a hidden browser running on the infected computer.

Technologies: operating-system, browser, remote-access

Products: macos, google-chrome, microsoft-edge, vivaldi, arc-browser, opera, brave-browser, chromium, apple-notes, apple-keychain, telegram

Vendors: apple, google, microsoft, vivaldi-technologies, the-browser-company, opera, brave-software, chromium-project, telegram, jamf

Large-scale DDoS attacks disrupted Threema secure messaging service — May Read

Threema suffered severe service disruptions after large-scale DDoS attacks hit its infrastructure and colocation partner, with attackers repeatedly changing tactics to evade mitigation. The company has added specialized upstream DDoS protection to reduce the risk of similar outages.

  • Multiple distributed denial-of-service attacks targeted the Threema secure messaging service earlier this week, causing severe disruptions to communications.
  • Threema said the attacks were difficult to defend against because the threat actor persisted for an extended period and continually changed tactics to circumvent mitigation measures.
  • The attacks targeted both Threema and its colocation partner, Nine, and Threema said it was not entirely clear whether it was the primary target or one of multiple targets.
  • Organizations using Threema On-Prem did not experience issues because they rely on their own infrastructure.
  • Threema implemented specialized DDoS protection to filter attack traffic upstream and reduce the load on its infrastructure.

Products: threema, threema-on-prem, threema-work

Vendors: threema, nine

item.title: Mexico Tax Authority Phishing Abuses Legitimate Yahoo Japan Mailbox
item.content:encoded:
Window: 16 Aug 10:00 → 16 Aug 14:00 UTC (4 hours)

Mexico's Tax Authority, Sent From a Yahoo Account — Should Read

Attackers impersonated Mexico’s tax authority using a real Yahoo Japan mailbox, so SPF, DKIM, DMARC and Microsoft composite authentication all passed while the actual identity claim was false. The phishing attempt relied on a clean PDF containing only a link to an aged dormant domain, showing why email authentication and file scanning alone can miss credential-harvesting lures.

  • A Spanish-language tax notice impersonating Mexico’s revenue service reached an accountant at a medical device manufacturer from a genuine free consumer Yahoo Japan mailbox.
  • SPF, DKIM, DMARC, and Microsoft composite authentication all passed because the message was sent through Yahoo Japan’s legitimate outbound infrastructure and was not spoofing the sender domain.
  • The display name and message body falsely claimed to represent the Mexican government and finance ministry, including a fabricated tax administration reference code.
  • The attached 3.2 KB PDF was structurally clean and contained only Spanish text instructing the recipient to click a link to view fiscal notification details.
  • The landing domain dyxcyk.com had been registered roughly eleven months before the message was sent and had no observed legitimate use, and Themis scored the message at 90% confidence for credential theft.

Technologies: email-security

Products: themis, adaptive-ai, outlook, yahoo-mail

Vendors: ironscales, microsoft, yahoo-japan
